title: Sudden pipe expansion, area ratio A1/A2=1/4 (ER=2 in diameter)
geometry: Two coaxial cylindrical pipes; upstream radius r1=0.5, downstream radius r2=1.0; sudden expansion at the joint plane; total length 12 diameters
question: Compute the pressure recovery coefficient Kp = (p_downstream - p_upstream) / (0.5 * rho * v1²) where p_upstream is sampled just upstream of the expansion and p_downstream is sampled far enough downstream that the recovery has stabilized.

reference.source: White, Fluid Mechanics 7e §6.10 (Borda-Carnot for sudden expansion)

notes: Closed-form Borda-Carnot: Kp = (1 - A1/A2)² = (1 - 0.25)² = 0.5625. ±5% relative absorbs entry-length effects + numerical dissipation. The case can be solved as 2D-axisymmetric (1-cell-thick wedge) or full-3D; both are valid.
